question: A pod stays Pending although nodes have free CPU and memory. What is the usual cause?
options: A node taint has no matching toleration
The readiness probe returned a 500 once
The container writes logs faster than fluentd
The deployment strategy is set to Recreate
explanation: Taints repel pods that do not tolerate them, whatever the spare capacity.

question: Why can a PodDisruptionBudget block a rolling node upgrade?
options: Draining would breach the minimum available
The budget forces pods onto spot instances
It rewrites the deployment update strategy
It holds the node in NotReady until quorum
explanation: Eviction is refused while removing a pod would take the deployment below minAvailable.

question: You ran commands on separate lines and one failed silently. What still ran?
options: Every following command, independently
Nothing, the shell aborts on first error
Only commands that read from standard input
Only the last command in the sequence block
explanation: Without && or set -e, each line runs regardless of the previous exit code.

question: A pod using an EBS volume is rescheduled into another availability zone. What happens?
options: It stays Pending, the volume is zone bound
It starts and the volume migrates with it
It starts with a fresh empty volume mounted
It fails with ImagePullBackOff on the node
explanation: An EBS volume lives in one availability zone, so the pod must schedule there.

question: A systemd service restarts cleanly but serves stale code. What was most likely missed?
options: The new files never reached the unit path
The unit needs a full daemon-reexec first
The service ran before journald had started
The restart policy was set to on-failure
explanation: A restart re-reads what is on disk; if the copy step failed, the old code is still there.
